Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime), none of them can proceed past the creation call, and zero required evidence is collected. This is a production API constraint failure localized to the eval probe org's agent quota, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so impact is scoped to the observability eval infrastructure.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on Agent Runtime Endpoint in production-api
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying HTTP 404, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner was unreachable at the time of the run. Because the stream terminated at generation_error before emitting any generation_completed frame or image URL, both required evidence items (frameTypes, imageUrlPresent) were never written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1416) issued an SSE request to /api/generate/image/stream, which internally attempted to open a session against the agent runtime harness. The harness returned HTTP 404, surfaced as SESSION_OPEN_FAILED in the generation_error frame. This prevented the stream from progressing past generation_start, so the runner's evidence-write at line 1430 (frameTypes and imageUrlPresent) was never reached. The failure is localized to the production-api runtime environment for this specific eval endpoint; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so this is an eval infrastructure failure, not a confirmed user-facing outage. The exact reason the harness returned 404 is uncertain: it could be a misconfigured or missing SWARM_BASE_URL/LOCAL_HARNESS_URL, a harness deployment that is absent or on an incompatible version, or a routing change that removed or relocated the endpoint the harness proxies to.

investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe for remote-agent-runtime calls createAgent as its first substantive action (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1350). Because agent creation failed, the probe could not proceed to the runtime test, no evidence was collected, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing. The same 409 body was returned for sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state, confirming the quota exhaustion is the shared upstream blocker for the entire remote-agents feature eval suite. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to indicate a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Swarm agent quota exhausted for the eval org: The production-api swarm enforces a hard limit of 100 agents per org. Prior eval runs, leaked agents from failed cleanup cycles, or accumulated probe agents that were not deleted may have consumed all 100 slots, causing every new POST /api/agents to return 409.

SECONDARY — Eval cleanup (withCleanup / track) failed in a prior run, leaving orphaned remote agents that count against the quota: The runner uses a withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1348). If cleanup did not execute (e.g., due to a prior crash or timeout), agents from previous probe runs accumulate and eventually exhaust the quota.

TERTIARY — The eval org's quota limit is set too low relative to the number of concurrent or sequential probe runs: If multiple observability workflow runs execute in parallel or in rapid succession, each creating agents before the previous run's cleanup completes, the quota can be transiently exhausted even without leaked agents.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit e7b1227 (fix(observability): read desktop shares from api origin, 2026-06-15T23:49:04Z) touched all three implicated eval files but its subject and touched paths (CI workflow files, not agent creation logic) do not match the 409 quota error; this commit is not supported as causal by the eval evidence.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on Agent Runtime Endpoint in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying HTTP 404, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner was unreachable at the time of the run. Because the stream terminated at generation_error before emitting any generation_completed frame or image URL, both required evidence items (frameTypes, imageUrlPresent) were never written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1416) issued an SSE request to /api/generate/image/stream, which internally attempted to open a session against the agent runtime harness. The harness returned HTTP 404, surfaced as SESSION_OPEN_FAILED in the generation_error frame. This prevented the stream from progressing past generation_start, so the runner's evidence-write at line 1430 (frameTypes and imageUrlPresent) was never reached. The failure is localized to the production-api runtime environment for this specific eval endpoint; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so this is an eval infrastructure failure, not a confirmed user-facing outage. The exact reason the harness returned 404 is uncertain: it could be a misconfigured or missing SWARM_BASE_URL/LOCAL_HARNESS_URL, a harness deployment that is absent or on an incompatible version, or a routing change that removed or relocated the endpoint the harness proxies to.

possibleCauses: (Most likely) The agent runtime harness is not deployed or not reachable at the URL resolved from LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL in the production-api eval environment, causing the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint to return 404 when it attempts to open a session.
(Likely) The harness is deployed but on an incompatible version whose session-open endpoint path has changed, so the 404 is a route mismatch rather than a missing deployment.

(Possible) The environment variables LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL are unset, empty, or pointing to a stale host in the CI/CD workflow that ran this eval, causing the API to fall back to a non-existent default route.

(Low confidence hypothesis) Commit e7b1227 ('fix(observability): read desktop shares from api origin') touched .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and setup-harness-sibling/action.yml; if those changes altered how the harness sibling is configured or started in the observability workflow, they could have introduced a misconfiguration. This is a low-confidence hypothesis because e7b1227's candidateTouchedPaths list is empty for the eval runner files and the commit subject does not directly reference image generation (suspect-change.e7b1227, confidence=low).

(Low confidence) The access token (args.token) was present (the runner did not return SKIP), but the token may lack the permission scope required to open an image-generation session, causing the backend to respond 404 instead of 401/403.
